title: The first carry
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies (the trilogy ran in print in three papers)
logline: Tuesday. The path again. This time Wood picks him up. The first carry. The dog, sixteen, allows it the way he allowed the lift across the channel in 2009: badly, then right. They go down.

panels.composition: The top of the gravel path. WOOD crouching. BARNABY on his feet. The beach below.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, a thin man crouching beside an old gray-muzzled dog at the top of a steep gravel path above a beach, no words

panels.composition: The lift. Badly — the dog's back legs hanging — then right, against the chest, the muzzle at the collarbone.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, a man lifting an old dog awkwardly then settling it against his chest with its muzzle at his collarbone, no words

panels.composition: Going down. The gravel. Wood's boots careful. The dog's eyes on the beach coming up.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, a man carrying an old dog carefully down a steep gravel path with the dog's eyes fixed on the beach below, no words

panels.composition: The beach. The dog set down on the sand at the bottom. Standing on it. The sea. Wood beside him, hands empty. They made it down.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, an old dog standing on wet sand at the foot of a bluff path beside a man with empty hands, the sea beyond, water bleeding into the ink, no words

notes: Wordless. The first carry. Badly, then right.
